chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sayf ibn 'Umaira, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is obligatory upon every believer who is our Shia to recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Surah As-Saff (referred to here as Asma Rabbika Al-A'la, i.e., As-Saff/Al-A'la contextually often linked or confused in transmission, but text says 'Subbhi' which is Al-A'la) in the night of Friday with Al-Jumu'ah and Subbhi Isma Rabbika Al-A'la, and in the noon prayer (Dhuhr) with Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun. When he does that, it is as if he is performing the deed of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and his reward and recompense is Paradise from Allah.
ai.seo_question: What are the obligatory Quranic recitations for Shia Muslims on Friday according to Thawab al-A'mal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this practice as a specific devotional obligation (wajib) for Shia believers, linking the recitation of these chapters to the commemoration of the Prophet and the Imams. By equating the reward to the Prophet's own deeds, the hadith emphasizes the spiritual merit of aligning one's Friday worship with the liturgical traditions of the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby reinforcing communal identity and piety.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Sayf b. ’Umayra from Mansur b. Hazim from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

“It is obligatory on every believer who is our Shia to recite Surah Juma and Surah Aala every Friday eve, and recite Surah Juma and Munafiqun in Friday noon prayer. A person doing so is like a person who is performing the deed of the Messenger of Allah (sw). The reward of this deed is that Allah would grant him Paradise.”
